problem.statement: WPF's internal event-locking code (ReaderWriterLockWrapper) allocates a huge number of Action objects on every PropertyChanged firing, causing blocking GC pauses that are only diagnosable by tracing a memory profiler down into WPF framework internals.

persona.primary: WPF application developer debugging UI performance/jank

context.situation: A developer building a fast-scrolling WPF image grid hit severe frame-rate drops that took a memory profiler and framework source inspection to trace to a WPF-internal locking pattern.

current_workarounds: Manually reduced allocations elsewhere in the app to offset GC pressure, improving performance from 10fps to 25fps
Used a memory profiler and read WPF reference source directly to trace allocations to the internal ReaderWriterLockWrapper class

possible_wedges.offer: Diagnostic tool that scans a running WPF app's allocations for known problematic framework-internal patterns (e.g. PropertyChanged-triggered ReaderWriterLockWrapper Action allocations) and flags root cause automatically.
Profiler plugin/rule pack that recognizes this specific WPF GC-storm signature and surfaces the root cause directly instead of requiring manual framework-source spelunking.
Static/dynamic analyzer for WPF codebases that flags high-frequency PropertyChanged usage on virtualized/ItemsControl grids as GC-storm risk before it hits production.

risks: Single evidence item (n=1); no corroborating reports of this exact pattern
No commercial intent or willingness-to-pay signal in the evidence (commercial_intent 0.1, commitment 0.05)
Only one persona/context observed: a solo developer debugging their own app, not a team or enterprise buyer
Evidence is a technical Q&A post, not a purchase inquiry, so demand for a paid tool is inferred, not stated
Unclear how common this specific high-frequency PropertyChanged + large virtualized grid scenario is outside this one app

cheapest_experiment.hypothesis: WPF developers hit by GC-pause jank from the PropertyChanged/ReaderWriterLockWrapper allocation storm would use a tool that auto-detects this specific framework pattern instead of manually tracing it via profiler + framework source.
cheapest_experiment.input: Publish a short technical writeup naming the exact issue (ReaderWriterLockWrapper Action allocations on PropertyChanged) in WPF dev forums/subreddits, with a landing page offering a free diagnostic script plus signup for an audit-tool waitlist.
cheapest_experiment.output: Landing page click-throughs and email/waitlist signups.
cheapest_experiment.commitment_event: Developer submits email or downloads the free diagnostic script.
cheapest_experiment.success_threshold: >=15 signups or downloads within 2 weeks from roughly 500 impressions.
cheapest_experiment.failure_threshold: <5 signups or downloads after 2 weeks despite comparable impressions.
